question: Martyrdom of revolutionary ___________ took place on 27 February, 1931.
solution:
The correct answer is **Chandrashekhar Azad.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **About Chandrashekhar Azad** 

 
 
• Chandrashekhar Azad was a fearless freedom fighter known for his role in the Kakori Conspiracy and other revolutionary activities.
 
• Azad was a key member of the HSRA and played a crucial role in planning and executing acts against the British government.
 
• His commitment to the cause was unwavering, and he preferred to die fighting rather than being captured by the British. He shot himself during a confrontation in Alfred Park, Allahabad, on **27 February 1931. **
 
 
 
• **​Batukeshwar Dutt **
 
 
• **​**Batukeshwar Dutt was a revolutionary who actively participated alongside Bhagat Singh in the protest against repressive laws by bombing the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929.
 
• He, along with Bhagat Singh, intentionally courted arrest to use the trial as a platform to promote their revolutionary ideals and criticize British imperialism.
 
• Dutt's act of nonviolent protest through hunger strikes during imprisonment became significant in the narrative of the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Sachindranath Sanyal **
 
 
• Sachindranath Sanyal was a key revolutionary and a mentor to many freedom fighters during the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was one of the founding members of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), which later became the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).
 
• Sanyal was instrumental in organizing and guiding revolutionary activities, including the Kakori Conspiracy of 1925.
 
• His role was crucial in shaping the ideology and strategy of the HSRA, which aimed at overthrowing British rule through armed struggle.
 
 
 
• Bhagat Singh
 
 
• Bhagat Singh was a prominent revolutionary and a charismatic leader in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He gained fame for his role in the protest against the Simon Commission and the bombing of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929.
 
• Bhagat Singh, along with Rajguru and Sukhdev, was sentenced to death in the Lahore Conspiracy Case.
 
• Their execution on 23 March 1931 galvanized public opinion and contributed significantly to the anti-colonial sentiment in India.
